_instructions: NETWORK: mainnet. Target: the mainnet Analytics dashboard (ask the admin for its uid). Do NOT paste this whole file into Grafana.

JOIN (verified against real data): streaming.msghash is BASE64 and equals mainnet_d.messages.hash_norm -- the NORMALIZED external hash. Both sides are emitted as lower(hex(base64Decode(...))), the 64-char form tonscan takes. Matched 180/180 on hash_norm and 0 on the raw hash. full_trace_time = max(now)-min(now) over mainnet_d.transactions grouped by trace_id; there is NO traces table on this cluster.

PICK A VARIANT BY THE DATASOURCE'S CH GRANTS -- that is the only difference. The panel chrome is byte-identical between them (type timeseries, drawStyle bars, unit s, the two colour/displayName overrides). variant_i_single_query_cross_db = ONE target on ONE datasource whose CH user must read BOTH dm_mainnet and mainnet_d, doing the join in SQL. variant_ii_two_datasource_DEPLOYABLE = TWO targets on two single-DB datasources under '-- Mixed --', joined in Grafana. On our cluster no single user reads both DBs (dm reads dm_mainnet only, vicread reads mainnet_d only), so variant i could not be run end to end here.

ONE X PER MESSAGE -- this is the load-bearing idea, do not undo it. Series A and B are two measurements of the SAME message, so they must share one x. A carries the send time (utime); B carries NO timestamp and is attached by joining on the message hash. Plotting the same message twice -- at utime and at the on-chain tx_now, 0-1s apart -- collapses Grafana's MINIMUM x-gap, and bar width is DERIVED from that gap (barWidthFactor only multiplies it; there is no absolute width setting). That is what rendered every bar as a hairline, and it flipped bars thin/thick between nearly identical windows depending on whether such a 1s pair fell inside. With one x per message the minimum gap is the real probe cadence (120 s here), so bars sit on their true timestamps at a stable width.

REJECTED DEAD ENDS, do not reintroduce: (1) quantizing ts onto a 20s lattice with toStartOfInterval + ORDER BY ts WITH FILL. It did make the width deterministic, but WITH FILL pads gaps with the column's TYPE DEFAULT, not NULL -- and max(now)-min(now) is a plain integer, so every empty slot became a real-looking full_trace_time of 0, i.e. a zero-height bar at timestamps where no message exists (measured 45 non-null rows for 22 real messages). (2) Making ts a STRING (toString/substring/concat), with or without the msghash appended as a label. Any string ts forces the panel to `barchart`, whose x is CATEGORICAL, so Grafana prints a label under EVERY bar -- at -45 degrees that is an unreadable smear filling half the panel. It also renders the label in the ClickHouse session timezone, so the axis disagreed with the time picker by 3 hours. The hash belongs ONLY in the table panel.

REPLACINGMERGETREE: the streaming table is keyed on (addr, utime), so a message can be present as several not-yet-merged versions that disagree -- one mainnet message had five rows, one of them still with finalized_action_in NULL while the others carried 0.733. They collapse once ClickHouse merges, but a query issued before that must not show the stale version, and two rows for one message would also put two points at one x (a 0s gap -> hairlines). Hence GROUP BY the message hash with argMax(finalized_action_in, updated_at): the latest version, which is what the merge would leave, and it skips NULLs so a finalized message is never drawn as unfinalized.

join_use_nulls = 1 IS REQUIRED. With ClickHouse's default an unmatched LEFT JOIN row yields the type default 0, not NULL -- so a streaming message with no on-chain trace would render as a genuine 'trace took 0 seconds'. The 0 is produced by the join, before the aggregate, so a cast cannot reach it.

ZOOM-INVARIANCE -- do NOT reintroduce an upper time bound on the transactions scan. full_trace_time must depend only on the trace, never on the panel window. Bounding by 'now <= $__toTime' truncates traces whose last hop lands after the window (under congestion the tail arrived over an hour after the external), so the SAME msghash read 42s zoomed in and 5303s zoomed out. Fix: anchor the trace set on monitor externals inside the window, KEEP the lower bound (the external is the trace's first tx, so the trace cannot start earlier), DROP the upper bound, and add trace_id IN (<same anchor>) to keep the unbounded scan cheap. Verified identical at 3h vs 20min windows.

OVERLAY: use joinByField mode 'inner'. An outer join keeps on-chain-only rows (a msghash the monitor never logged), fills their ts with 0, and Grafana plots that at 1970 -- a permanent 'Data outside time range' overlay that cannot be filtered away (the join fills 0, not SQL NULL). Inner drops those rows; in a 3h window that was 3 of 265 on testnet and 0 of 90 on mainnet, all at the window edges.

MONITOR WALLET: '0:086CA3CDAE529602F9C9C13826481D79DF2473851B0A9B4EA334ABF61F4B4AEA'. The monitor's externals have no fixed opcode, so the destination is the stable filter. If the monitor rotates wallets, refresh it: take recent streaming msghashes and run  SELECT destination, count() FROM mainnet_d.messages WHERE lower(hex(base64Decode(toString(hash_norm)))) IN (<hashes>) AND direction='in' AND source IS NULL GROUP BY destination ORDER BY 2 DESC.

SWAP DATASOURCE UIDS: variant ii uses the local preview uids 'dmmainnetch' (dm_mainnet) and 'mainnetdch' (mainnet_d). Replace with your prod uids -- one CH datasource per DB/user. variant i uses ff5z8xz8e1urke.
UNITS: finalized_action_in is Nullable(Float64) SECONDS; panel unit 's' is correct, no /1000.

READING IT: the point is the contrast. During the 31.08 testnet load run most probes had NULL finalized_action_in (13.6% present in the last hour, 0% in the last 30 minutes) while their on-chain traces had long completed -- streaming lagged 8-11 minutes behind a chain that was keeping up.

ZEROS ARE REAL, not missing data. On an idle chain full_trace_time is 0 almost everywhere: the indexer runs 1-3s behind, the traces are complete (5 transactions, no unconsumed out-messages), and all five land in the same second. `now` is the block's gen_utime in WHOLE SECONDS, so 1s is the resolution floor and a sub-second trace can only read 0. Under load the same traces stretched to thousands of seconds.

IN-FLIGHT CAVEAT: a trace whose tail has not landed when the query runs reads SHORT and grows on a later refresh -- it is measuring an unfinished trace, not a fast one. No query change can fix it (the tail does not exist yet); distinguishing it would need a completeness check, e.g. requiring every out-message of the trace to have a matching in-tx.

PERF (measured on testnet under ~5M tx/h): the zoom-invariant on-chain query ran 94ms over a 3h window and 74ms over 20 minutes; the streaming query ~6ms. Dropping the upper bound did NOT make it slower -- the trace_id IN anchor prunes the scan.

TABLE (panel 6): add tr.full_trace_time to its SELECT and splice the LEFT JOIN block (table_column_addition__left_join_block) before its WHERE; alias streaming as s and prefix its columns with s. Do NOT dedupe the table the way the chart does -- there a duplicate row is itself worth seeing, and silently picking one of two disagreeing rows could show a message as unfinalized when it finalized.

variant_i_single_query_cross_db.title: Jetton Transfer time
variant_i_single_query_cross_db.description: full_trace_time = on-chain trace span (last tx block time - first tx block time, as in tonscan). finalized_action_in = when got finalized action from toncenter's streaming. [variant i: single query; datasource CH user must have grants on BOTH dm_mainnet and mainnet_d]

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  /* ONE x per message: the real, UNQUANTIZED send time. The on-chain value is attached by joining
     on the message identity, so a message is never plotted at two different x values -- that
     double-plotting is what collapsed Grafana's minimum x-gap (bar width is derived from it) and
     squashed every bar to a hairline. Nothing is quantized, filled or smoothed. */
  fromUnixTimestamp(toInt64(min(s.utime)))       AS ts,
  argMax(s.finalized_action_in, s.updated_at)    AS finalized_action_in,
  max(tr.full_trace_time)                        AS full_trace_time
FROM dm_mainnet.toncenter_streaming_mainnet AS s
  INNER JOIN
  (
    SELECT
      lower(hex(base64Decode(toString(m.hash_norm)))) AS msghash_hex,
      d.full_trace_time AS full_trace_time
    FROM
    (
      SELECT hash_norm, tx_trace_id
      FROM mainnet_d.messages
      WHERE direction = 'in' AND source IS NULL
        AND destination = '0:086CA3CDAE529602F9C9C13826481D79DF2473851B0A9B4EA334ABF61F4B4AEA'  /* monitor sender wallet */
        AND tx_now >= toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime)
        AND tx_now <= toUnixTimestamp($__toTime)
    ) AS m
    INNER JOIN
    (
      /* ZOOM-INVARIANT: lower bound kept, upper bound DROPPED, trace_id IN (<anchor>) */
      SELECT trace_id, max(now) - min(now) AS full_trace_time
      FROM mainnet_d.transactions
      WHERE now >= toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime) - 300
        AND trace_id IN (
          SELECT tx_trace_id FROM mainnet_d.messages
          WHERE direction = 'in' AND source IS NULL
            AND destination = '0:086CA3CDAE529602F9C9C13826481D79DF2473851B0A9B4EA334ABF61F4B4AEA'
            AND tx_now >= toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime) - 300
            AND tx_now <= toUnixTimestamp($__toTime)
        )
      GROUP BY trace_id
    ) AS d ON m.tx_trace_id = d.trace_id
  ) AS tr ON lower(hex(base64Decode(s.msghash))) = tr.msghash_hex
WHERE $__timeFilter(fromUnixTimestamp(toInt64(s.utime)))
/* GROUP BY the message: the streaming table is a ReplacingMergeTree keyed on (addr, utime), so a
   message can appear as several not-yet-merged versions that disagree -- one mainnet message had
   five rows, one of them still with finalized_action_in NULL. argMax(..., updated_at) takes the
   latest version, i.e. what the merge would eventually leave, and skips NULLs. */
GROUP BY lower(hex(base64Decode(s.msghash)))
ORDER BY ts
LIMIT 60000
SETTINGS join_use_nulls = 1   /* unmatched join row -> NULL, not a fabricated 0 */

variant_ii_two_datasource_DEPLOYABLE.title: Jetton Transfer time
variant_ii_two_datasource_DEPLOYABLE.description: full_trace_time = on-chain trace span (last tx block time - first tx block time, as in tonscan). finalized_action_in = when got finalized action from toncenter's streaming. [variant ii: A=dm_mainnet streaming, B=mainnet_d on-chain, joined in Grafana on the message hash]

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  /* ONE x per message: the real, UNQUANTIZED send time. Series B carries NO timestamp -- the
     Grafana join on msghash attaches its value to this row, so a message has exactly one x. */
  fromUnixTimestamp(toInt64(min(utime)))  AS ts,
  lower(hex(base64Decode(msghash)))       AS msghash_hex,   /* join key only, hidden in the panel */
  argMax(finalized_action_in, updated_at) AS finalized_action_in
FROM dm_mainnet.toncenter_streaming_mainnet
WHERE $__timeFilter(fromUnixTimestamp(toInt64(utime)))
/* see the ReplacingMergeTree note in variant i */
GROUP BY msghash_hex
ORDER BY ts
LIMIT 60000

SELECT
  /* streaming.msghash (base64) == mainnet_d.messages.hash_norm; both sides emit
     lower(hex(base64Decode(...))), the same key the table panel uses. No timestamp here. */
  lower(hex(base64Decode(toString(m.hash_norm)))) AS msghash_hex,
  max(d.full_trace_time)                          AS full_trace_time
FROM
(
  SELECT hash_norm, tx_trace_id
  FROM mainnet_d.messages
  WHERE direction = 'in' AND source IS NULL
    AND destination = '0:086CA3CDAE529602F9C9C13826481D79DF2473851B0A9B4EA334ABF61F4B4AEA'  /* monitor sender wallet */
    AND tx_now >= toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime)
    AND tx_now <= toUnixTimestamp($__toTime)
) AS m
INNER JOIN
(
  /* ZOOM-INVARIANT: keep the LOWER bound (the external is the trace's first tx, so the trace
     cannot start earlier) but DROP the upper bound so a tail landing hours later is counted.
     trace_id IN (<same anchor>) keeps it cheap. */
  SELECT trace_id, max(now) - min(now) AS full_trace_time
  FROM mainnet_d.transactions
  WHERE now >= toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime) - 300
    AND trace_id IN (
      SELECT tx_trace_id FROM mainnet_d.messages
      WHERE direction = 'in' AND source IS NULL
        AND destination = '0:086CA3CDAE529602F9C9C13826481D79DF2473851B0A9B4EA334ABF61F4B4AEA'
        AND tx_now >= toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime) - 300
        AND tx_now <= toUnixTimestamp($__toTime)
    )
  GROUP BY trace_id
) AS d ON m.tx_trace_id = d.trace_id
GROUP BY msghash_hex
LIMIT 60000

modified_table_panel_id6.title: TX hashes
modified_table_panel_id6.description: REFERENCE ONLY - merge the full_trace_time column + the LEFT JOIN block into your live panel 6; keep its other columns/options. Uses the single-query cross-DB form (variant i); if the datasource cannot read both DBs, build the table the same two-datasource way as variant ii.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  fromUnixTimestamp(toInt64(s.utime)) AS ts,
  lower(hex(base64Decode(s.msghash))) AS msghash_hex,   /* paste this into tonscan */
  s.msghash                           AS msghash_base64,
  tr.full_trace_time                  AS full_trace_time
  /* keep your existing panel-6 columns here, e.g. s.finalized_action_in, s.finalized_tx_in, ... */
FROM dm_mainnet.toncenter_streaming_mainnet AS s
  LEFT JOIN
  (
    SELECT
      arrayJoin([toString(m.hash), toString(m.hash_norm)]) AS msghash,
      d.full_trace_time AS full_trace_time
    FROM
    (
      SELECT hash, hash_norm, tx_trace_id
      FROM mainnet_d.messages
      WHERE direction = 'in' AND source IS NULL
        AND destination = '0:086CA3CDAE529602F9C9C13826481D79DF2473851B0A9B4EA334ABF61F4B4AEA'  /* monitor sender wallet */
        AND tx_now >= toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime) - 300
        AND tx_now <= toUnixTimestamp($__toTime)
    ) AS m
    INNER JOIN
    (
      /* ZOOM-INVARIANT: keep the LOWER bound (the external is the trace's first tx, so the
         trace cannot start earlier) but DROP the upper bound, so a tail landing hours after
         the external is still fully counted. Without this, max(now)-min(now) is truncated by
         the panel window and the SAME msghash changes value when you zoom.
         trace_id IN (<same anchor>) keeps the unbounded scan cheap. */
      SELECT trace_id, max(now) - min(now) AS full_trace_time
      FROM mainnet_d.transactions
      WHERE now >= toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime) - 300
        AND trace_id IN (
          SELECT tx_trace_id FROM mainnet_d.messages
          WHERE direction = 'in' AND source IS NULL
            AND destination = '0:086CA3CDAE529602F9C9C13826481D79DF2473851B0A9B4EA334ABF61F4B4AEA'
            AND tx_now >= toUnixTimestamp($__fromTime) - 300
            AND tx_now <= toUnixTimestamp($__toTime)
        )
      GROUP BY trace_id
    ) AS d ON m.tx_trace_id = d.trace_id
  ) AS tr ON s.msghash = tr.msghash
WHERE $__timeFilter(fromUnixTimestamp(toInt64(s.utime)))
ORDER BY ts DESC
LIMIT 60000
SETTINGS join_use_nulls = 1   /* unmatched LEFT JOIN -> NULL, not a fabricated 0 */
